plain_english: Nick's India Stock Desk is a research screen for NSE stocks. It does not place trades and it does not connect to a broker. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell.

There are no option contract picks. The liquid stocks page is a stock screen. The put and call walls page is market mood only. Indian options use fixed lot sizes, so this desk does not pick a contract.

Prices are in rupees. The daily bars come from the NSE bhavcopy. If that file is missing, the desk tries the BSE bhavcopy, then Stooq, then Yahoo. The Nifty 50, SENSEX, and Bank Nifty are shown side by side. SENSEX daily bars come from the BSE index file, then Yahoo, then Stooq, then the saved cache. NSE stocks are compared with the Nifty 50. BSE-only stocks are compared with SENSEX. Turn SENSEX off with feature.sensex.

Each money measure is plus 1, 0, or minus 1 versus that company's own recent history. Lower is better for forward P/E, trailing P/E, price/sales, debt/equity, and price/free cash flow. Higher is better for revenue growth, EPS growth, return on equity, and dividend yield. Analyst rating can be plus 2 to minus 2. Shareholding, insiders, the price trend, the oscillator, the latest result, and the sector each add a small point. The score is the sum of the points we actually have.
A missing number is left blank and marked n/a. It is not stored as zero and it does not add or subtract a point. If a free source is blocked, the page says not available.
Free data does not include a history of forward estimates. The baseline for forward P/E is the 3-year average of year-end trailing P/E.
The industry figure is the middle value of the other stocks in the same sector on this desk. It is not a paid database. If fewer than four peers have a number, the comparison is blank.

BUY, HOLD, and AVOID are research labels. A high score that is extended, in a downtrend, or missing most of its financials is labeled HOLD instead of BUY. When a stock has no financials yet, the label is Not scored yet, in gray, and the reason says financials are still downloading. That is not an AVOID. Entry, stop, and target are a plan for study, not an order.

You will see an analyst target when Yahoo has one, a price/free-cash-flow target, a PEG-style target, and a blend of whichever of those exist. The trade target is separate. It is an entry-zone plan using the recent daily range.

Once a month the job asks what the score would have been using only data that was already public, then looks at the next 1, 4, and 12 weeks versus the Nifty 50. Read the headline. If it says there is no clear edge, believe that. Past results are not future results.

Promoter, FII, DII, and other public percents come from the NSE shareholding filing when that file is reachable. The change is versus the prior quarter. If the split is missing, the cell says not verified. It is not a US 13F report.
Insider points use NSE PIT buy and sell counts over three months. If NSE blocks the file, the page says data not available for free and the score for that piece stays blank.

The put/call line is Nifty put open interest divided by call open interest, when the NSE option chain answers. Walls are the strikes with the most open interest. They are mood, not a trade. If NSE blocks the chain, the page says not available.
There is no Indian version of the AAII survey, so that survey is not shown. This page uses India VIX and, when the NSE file answers, the day's FII and DII cash flow in crores.
There is no free official daily Nifty 50 P/E this desk can rely on. The chart is the median trailing P/E of the stocks on this desk. The official column stays blank.

The macro page shows India CPI, GDP, and industry growth from the World Bank when that feed answers, plus the rupee from Yahoo. A forecast is often missing, so the surprise stays blank. It is a sketch, not a forecast. The rate column on the sector map is a simple rule of thumb.
This is the Nifty Auto index divided by the Nifty FMCG index. It stands in for the old discretionary versus staples chart. Above the 50-day average of the ratio is labeled risk on.

The after-close run reads that day's bhavcopy and a slice of statements and shareholding. It does not download every company from Yahoo. A light morning run only refreshes headlines and FII or DII cash. If a source fails, the previous file is kept and the updates log says CACHED.

The desk covers NSE shares and BSE-only shares. Tags are Nifty 50, Next 50, Midcap 150, Smallcap 250, Microcap 250, Total Market, Other NSE, and BSE only. Each tag has a switch. SME is off unless you turn it on. Your holdings, watchlist, and my picks are always included. A company on both exchanges is shown once, under the NSE symbol.

Scanners hide names whose 20-day median traded value is under the rupee line in config.json. The line is 1 crore rupees unless you change it. Top stocks can still show the quieter names if you turn the liquid filter off.

The FII and DII page shows cash-market buy and sell in crore rupees. Green is net buying. Red is net selling. The history grows each day. A second block shows index-futures positioning when the NSE participant file answers.
Times are shown in India time (IST) and Pacific time (PT).

This page follows the same 8-point trend template and pullback count as Nick's indicator. NSE stocks use the Nifty 50 as the benchmark. BSE-only stocks use SENSEX. A stock is listed only when it would get the green VCP tag: all 8 trend rules pass and there are at least two pullbacks that get smaller. READY means price is still under the buy line. BROKEN OUT today means today's close went above the buy line on volume at least 1.5 times the 50-day average. WATCHING means price is above the buy line on low volume, or there is only one pullback so far, and the trend is still 8 of 8. A stock still in a trade stays listed if its buy printed with 8 of 8, even if the trend has slipped since. Set vcp.show_weaker_trend to true to also see stocks with smaller pullbacks but a weaker trend. They show as WATCHING (trend not 8/8).

C and A are the year-ago EPS change from the saved statements. N is how close the price is to its 52-week closing high. S is the 20-day average volume. L is the relative-strength percentile versus the Nifty for NSE stocks, and versus SENSEX for BSE-only stocks. I is the shareholding change when we have it. M shows the Nifty 50, SENSEX, and Bank Nifty side by side as Uptrend, Under pressure, or Correction. The market is in an uptrend when the Nifty 50 or SENSEX is in an uptrend. Set market.require_both_uptrends to true to require both. Bank Nifty is shown and does not decide. The What CANSLIM means box explains each letter. A blank that says not verified was not in the cache. It is not a guess.

On a stock list, the button at the left of a row opens that stock's daily price chart under the row. Only one chart stays open. The caption names the benchmark: Nifty 50 for NSE stocks, SENSEX for BSE-only stocks. The scorecard says the same thing. Turn the charts off with feature.row_charts in config.json.

The 52-week high is the highest price of the last 252 trading sessions, and the 52-week low is the lowest. A new high today means the close is at or above the prior 252-session high. A new low today means the close is at or below the prior 252-session low. Near the high means the close is within 5% of that high. A high on volume also needs volume at least 1.5 times the 50-day average. This page is separate from the 52-week breakouts list, which only keeps names within 1% of the high. Research only. Turn it off with feature.scanner_52w.

Research list, not a recommendation. This desk never places trades. A stock is listed when VCP, Box, Flag, Qullamaggie, Marios, Episodic Pivot (EP), or CANSLIM is ready or broke out today, the close is above the 50-day and the 200-day averages, and the risk from the entry to the stop is 8% or less. Qullamaggie, Marios, and EP rows marked Too wide, skip are left out. An EP counts as ready on its EP day and days 2 to 5 (buy above the EP-day high), and as broke out today when the price goes above it. EP stocks locked at the upper circuit, faded EPs, and delayed EPs are left out. Chart setups only, on while financials coverage is under 80%, also keeps a BUY or a Not scored yet label and marks the unscored names Financials pending. A scored AVOID stays off the list until you press Show anyway. Turn that switch off and the page keeps only BUY. The market check passes when the Nifty 50 or SENSEX is in an uptrend. Set market.require_both_uptrends to require both. Bank Nifty is shown and does not decide. When the check fails, the list stays empty until you press Show anyway. Show anyway then lists every name that passes the chart rules, greyed out, with its real verdict: BUY, HOLD, AVOID, or Not scored yet. The banner names which index is up or down. The stop is the tighter of 7% under the entry or the setup's own stop. Target 1 is 20% above the entry, or 20% above the breakout close. Target 2 is the entry plus three times the risk. Scores are rebuilt from the saved financials and shareholding at the end of every backfill run, with no new downloads. Turn that off with fundamentals_backfill.rebuild_pages_after_run. Turn the page off with feature.buy_setups.

The Trading Floor is a short desk debate about today's top picks: the Buy setups list in its own order, topped up with stocks that are ready or broke out today on at least two pattern scanners, 15 stocks at most. Six roles each write one line. News says why it may be moving, from headlines already saved (3 days). Scout compares today's volume with the 50 sessions before it, using the bhavcopy volume the desk already has. Charts reads the entry, stop, and target the desk already worked out. Skeptic argues against the trade. Sentiment says whether the crowd is too hot. Each of those five gives +1, 0, or -1, and the Chief adds them up: 2 or more with no hard no from the Skeptic is Buy, 0 or 1 is Wait, under 0 is Skip, and a Charts veto (no usable levels, or the price already under the stop) is always Skip. The page also shows that day's FII and DII cash flow. Tap a stock to see its chart with the entry, stop, and target lines. Advice only: it never places an order, never calls a broker, and sends no alerts. It runs on the main update after the NSE bhavcopy is in (3:00 AM PT). Turn it off with feature.trading_floor.

News: +1 when the fresh headlines that name the stock lean positive, -1 when they lean negative, 0 when mixed or when there are none (the line then says No fresh headlines found). Scout: +1 at 1.5 times normal volume on an up day, or 3 or more days in a row above normal; -1 at 1.5 times normal on a down day, or under 0.7 times normal; else 0. Charts: veto when there is no valid entry, stop, and target or the price is at or under the stop; +1 when reward/risk is at least 2 and the stop is 8% or less below the entry; else 0. Skeptic: one objection each for no fresh news, volume under 0.8 times normal, 10% or more over the 20-day average (or 25% over the 50-day), 5% or more over the entry, the Nifty 50 and SENSEX not in an uptrend, and earnings within 7 days. No objections is +1, one is 0, two or more is -1; three or more, or 10% over the entry, is a hard no. Sentiment: one hot flag each for up 15% in 5 days, 8% over MA10, 12% over MA20, a 5% gap up today, 6 up days in a row, and 5 or more fresh headlines. No flags is +1, one is 0, two or more is -1. FII and DII cash is shown with the call and does not add a point. The full rules are in docs/trading_floor_rules.md.

News reuses the headlines the desk already stores. A market headline counts when it names the stock. Only picks with none of those get one request each to the free Google News RSS search (no key), on the main run after the bhavcopy, once a day, so at most 15 requests a day. Nothing extra is asked of Yahoo, and no new volume file is downloaded. The answers are kept in cache/trading_floor_news.csv. A failed request is soft: that stock says No fresh headlines found and the Skeptic counts it.

feature.trading_floor turns the page and its headline requests on or off. The trading_floor block in config.json holds every number: max_stocks, fill_from_scanners and fill_min_scanners, and one group each for news, scout, charts, skeptic, sentiment, and verdict. Each role has an on switch (off means it votes 0 and says Off in Settings) and each check has its own switch, such as trading_floor.skeptic.market_check or trading_floor.sentiment.gap_check. verdict.buy_min_total (2) and verdict.wait_min_total (0) are the Chief's cutoffs.

FAKE MONEY. The Paper Test follows the Trading Floor's Buy calls with Rs 10,00,000 of pretend cash, so you can see if the calls would have made or lost money. No real order is ever placed, no broker is connected, and no alert is sent. Each new Buy call is bought at the next session's open from the bhavcopy, with Rs 1,00,000 (10% of the starting cash), in fractional shares, with at most 10 stocks at once. It never borrows. A call is skipped when the stock is already held or when there is no cash left, and the page says why. The test starts on the first main run that has it and only moves forward. Nothing is replayed. The chart compares the fake account with putting the same Rs 10,00,000 into the Nifty 50 on the start day. Turn it off with feature.trading_floor_paper.

Stop and target are the Trading Floor's, frozen on the day of the call. Each daily bar from the entry day on is checked in this order: opened at or under the stop, sold at the open; opened at or over the target, sold at the open; the high and low touched both the stop and the target on the same day, counted as the stop to stay careful; the low touched the stop, sold at the stop; the high touched the target, sold at the target; after 20 trading days (the entry day is day 1), sold at that day's close. A stock that opens past its stop or target on the buy day is not bought. Win rate counts a closed trade with a gain as a win. A flat trade counts as a loss. Rules: docs/trading_floor_paper_rules.md.

feature.trading_floor_paper turns the page and the daily update on or off. Off leaves the saved paper files as they are. The trading_floor_paper block in config.json holds start_cash (1000000), position_pct (10), max_open (10), time_stop_days (20), fractional_shares (on), share_decimals (4), skip_if_held (on), and skip_gap_past_plan (on). The state is saved in data/paper_trades.csv, data/paper_equity.csv, and data/paper_summary.csv so it survives a restart. Only the main run after the bhavcopy, and the late bhavcopy retry, change them. Running the same day twice changes nothing. The morning run leaves them alone.

The graph compares Nifty sector indexes with a benchmark using daily closes already in the cache. The default benchmark is the Nifty 50. You can switch the page to SENSEX. No new download. RS is the sector index close divided by that benchmark. RS-Ratio is 100 plus the z-score of that ratio, after a moving average, versus its own rolling mean. RS-Momentum is 100 plus the z-score of the change in RS-Ratio. 100 is the center. Leading is top right, Weakening is bottom right, Lagging is bottom left, Improving is top left. Weekly and monthly points are built from those same daily bars. The score blends relative strength, how many of the sector's stocks are above their averages, how many are near a 52-week high, how many are on a buy setup, and the average desk score. A missing factor is left out. It is not stored as zero. Oil and gold are not on file. Turn it off with feature.sector_rotation.

A separate job downloads company statements, ratios, analyst numbers, and promoter, FII, DII, and public shareholding. It is scheduled every 15 minutes, including weekends, and continues from a saved cursor. GitHub may start a run late. Liquid stocks come first, then the rest of the NSE list, then BSE-only names. After every name has a saved row, it refreshes the oldest shareholding about every 90 days and refreshes results after the next earnings date, or every 90 days. At 200 statements and 200 shareholding names a run, the first pass of the full list is well under a day when the free sources answer. A name with no shareholding filing is saved for later in the pass. Turn it off with feature.fundamentals_backfill. The price schedule does not change.

GitHub's own timer often starts this desk's scheduled updates hours late, or skips them, so the desk keeps its own clock. One small keeper job is always running in the Actions tab (named Update keeper). It waits until 10 minutes after each update time (08:00, 16:30, and 18:30 IST, Monday to Friday, NSE trading holidays skipped; in Pacific time 6:30 PM the evening before, then 3:00 AM and 5:00 AM, each an hour later in summer time) and, if that update did not run, starts exactly that one. 45 minutes after each update time it checks that the update worked. A failed morning or close update gets one more try, never more. For the close and the 18:30 IST retry it also checks that the prices reached that day (price_as_of in meta.json); if not, it writes a warning in the keeper run, and the 18:30 IST retry is the second look. The 18:30 IST retry is skipped when the close already brought that day's prices. It never starts two updates within 50 minutes, and when GitHub's late timer fires afterwards, that run stops after a few seconds because the slot already ran. Every 5.5 hours the keeper starts the next keeper and stops. Every update and watchdog run also starts a keeper if none is running. It downloads no market data. The switch is self_heal_keeper in config.json; the timings are in the keeper block (check_after_min 10, verify_after_min 45, recheck_min 15, chunk_min 330, min_gap_min 50, max_tries 2). Turn it off and the keeper stops at its next check and the watchdog takes over the daily update again.

This page lists stocks that traded far more shares than usual in the latest session. Volume ratio is today's volume divided by the average of the last 50 sessions, so 3.2x means 3.2 times a normal day. Heavy volume on an up day usually means buying. Heavy volume on a down day usually means selling. The page starts at 2x or more, a close over Rs 20, and at least Rs 1 crore traded. You can switch to 1.5x, 3x, or 5x, pick up days or down days, and pick NSE or BSE. Tap a row to see its chart. It uses the same daily prices the desk already saves. No new download. ETFs and funds are left out. Research only. Turn it off with feature.high_volume_scanner.
A box is a tight sideways range that closes out the top on above-average volume. A flag is a sharp rise, a short pause, then a close above the pause on volume. These two are desk rules.

Qullamaggie's own rules: top 1 to 2% gainers, ADR of 3.5 to 5% or more, a 30 to 100% run in 1 to 3 months, then a 2 week to 2 month base with higher lows riding the 10 and 20-day averages (sometimes the 50). He buys the opening range high, puts the stop at the low of the day no wider than ADR, sells 1/3 to 1/2 after 3 to 5 days, moves the stop to breakeven, and trails the rest with the 10 or 20-day close. Daily-data approximations on this page: top 3% on the 21, 63 or 126-day return across the scanned stocks, a 30% run within the 63 days before the base that rose in 40 days or less, ADR as the 20-day average of high divided by low minus 1 (3.5% or more, 5% or more is tagged fast), price at least Rs 20, a 10 to 40 day base whose second-half lowest low is at or above the first half, at least 70% of closes above the 20-day or all above the 50-day, and the 10-day above the 20-day with both rising. Desk rules with their own switches: base no deeper than 25%, base top within 10% of the run high, and the base starts in the top half of its range. The trigger is the day's high going above the base high when the prior day's high was not. Fill is the open or the base high, whichever is higher. Stop is that day's low. More than 1 ADR from fill to stop is Too wide, skip, and it stays on the page but not on Buy setups. 0.5 ADR or less is A+. ADR is used for this check on both pages. READY means the close is within 1 ADR under the base high. Volume of 1.5 times the prior 50 days is a ranking flag, not a rule. Volume drying up is shown as a flag. IN TRADE follows each breakout bar by bar: Sell 1/3 to 1/2 on day 3 to 5 with the stop at breakeven, then the first close under the 10-day ends it (qullamaggie.trail_use_sma20 switches to the 20-day). CLOSED shows the reason and the date, for up to 60 sessions. Market light, results within 5 sessions, 20-day traded value, price band, and shares for 0.5% risk are columns, not rules. Every rule has a switch in the qullamaggie block of config.json.

Marios Stamatoudis's own rules: ADR above 2.5% (he prefers 3.5%), opening range breakout entries, a stop at the low of the day under 1 ATR, partials at 2.5 to 3 ADRs above the entry (ADRs, not R), breakeven after the partial, and a trail on the 10, 20 or 50-day average. The slides that went around were Financial Wisdom TV's summary, not his own. This page uses the same daily-data base and entry checks as the Qullamaggie page, with ADR at least 2.5% (3.5% or more marked preferred), a prior run within 126 days, and the volume dry-up as a rule (last 5 base days under the 50-day average). The stop check uses ADR instead of ATR. A weak day-1 close (under the fill, or less than half the risk above it) is flagged. Selling: 1/4 to 1/3 when the high reaches the entry plus 2.5 ADRs (the 3 ADR level is shown too), then the stop moves to breakeven. A close under the 10-day sells 1/3 of the rest. A close under the 20-day sells the rest and the trade shows as CLOSED with the reason and date. Every rule has a switch in the marios block of config.json.

An Episodic Pivot (EP) is a big jump on surprise news, like strong results. This page follows Qullamaggie and Stockbee's own rules. An EP day is a gap up of 10% or more at the open, or a close 8% or more above the day before, on at least 3 times the average volume of the last 50 days. Price must be at least Rs 20. Only liquid stocks are scanned (at least Rs 1 crore a day, the middle value of the last 20 days). ETFs and funds are left out. Prices are end of day only, so there is no early-morning check and no opening range high. EP TODAY means a strong close: in the top half of the day's range and at or above the open. Buy above the EP-day high in the next sessions, with the stop at the EP-day low. EP FADED means a weak close, so it is not a buy. WATCHING is day 2 to 5 after a strong EP. DELAYED WATCH is day 6 to 20 (day 2 to 20 after a fade): it waits for a tight 5-day range and buys above its high. BROKEN OUT today means the price went above the buy level today. IN TRADE shows the stop. On day 3 to 5 of the trade it says SELL PART: sell 1/3 to 1/2 and move the stop to breakeven. Then sell the rest on the first close under the 10-day average, or the 20-day when the normal daily move (ADR) is under 5%. NO FOLLOW-THROUGH means it did not rise one normal day's move in 5 sessions (Stockbee's time stop). CLOSED shows the result and stays for 10 sessions. A stock locked at the upper circuit is flagged no entry possible. A stop more than 1.5 times the normal daily range is marked Too wide, skip. Rows are ranked by base grade: A is flat or down before the EP, B is up a little, C already ran more than 30% in 3 months. Earnings EP means results came out on the EP day or the day before. Guidance, revenue beats, and other news are not in the free data, so check them with the announcements link. Nick's own filters are switches that start off. Numbers are under episodic_pivot in config.json. Turn the page off with feature.scanner_episodic_pivot.

The Gap Up page lists stocks that opened above the day before's high (a true gap) and have held it since. The gap must be at least 3%. Gap % is the open divided by the day before's high, minus 1. Turn the 3% minimum off with gap_up.min_gap_filter, and then any gap counts. The gap day also needs at least 1.5 times the average volume of the 50 days before it and a close of at least Rs 20. The stock must also trade at least Rs 1 crore a day on average over the last 50 days, the same rupee line the Episodic Pivot scan uses. ETFs and funds are left out. The gap-day low is the hold level. A stock is dropped as soon as any daily close from the gap day through today is below it. A close exactly on it still counts as holding. Only gaps in the last 21 trading days, today included, are checked. If a stock gapped more than once, the most recent gap that still holds is shown. GAP UP today means the gap was on the latest day. GAP HOLDING means an older gap that still holds. Newest gaps come first, then the biggest. Close in gap-day range shows where the gap day closed between its low (0) and high (100). Also on lists the other scanners that show the same stock. Gap Up does not feed Buy setups. Prices are end of day only. It uses the saved daily bars. Nothing new is downloaded, and nothing is sent to you. Numbers are under gap_up in config.json. Turn the page off with feature.scanner_gap_up.

Market cap is the number of shares times the latest close, in Rs crore. Share counts come from the company results the desk already saved, and they are kept in cache/market_cap.csv so every run reuses them. A newer result replaces an older count. If an Episodic Pivot stock still has no share count, the after-close run asks Yahoo for it, at most 5 stocks a run, and saves the answer. A stock with no answer is asked again after 30 days. No paid data and no key. A share split after the last result can make the number too low until the next result.

The Chart Viewer page shows one big daily chart at a time. Pick a list at the top. All scanner stocks is every stock on VCP, CANSLIM, Box, Flag, Qullamaggie, Marios, Episodic Pivot, Gap Up, Leaders, 52-week, 52-week breakouts, High volume, Pullbacks, Growth, Quality, Dividend, or Liquid stocks, with no repeats. Chart scanners count every status except CLOSED (chart_viewer.include_watching and chart_viewer.include_closed). Growth, Quality, Dividend, Liquid stocks, and Pullbacks count the stocks that pass. High volume counts the stocks its page lists. 52-week counts a new high, a new low, or near the high. Gap Up counts every stock its page lists (chart_viewer.include_gap_up). Buy setups and the watchlist show in the reason box but do not add to the count. Stocks found by the most scanners come first, then the strongest. A Technical | Fundamental switch sits above the list (chart_viewer.group_toggle). Technical shows only the chart scanners and All technical stocks. Fundamental shows only CANSLIM, Leaders, Growth, Quality and Dividend, and All fundamental stocks. The reason box then lists only that group's scanners, plus Buy setups and the watchlist. The switch starts on Technical (chart_viewer.default_group) and remembers your last choice on this device. Swiping stays inside the list you picked. You can also pick one scanner, Buy setups, or your watchlist. Each scanner page has an Open in Chart Viewer link. Tap Full screen. On iPhone, where Safari has no full screen for pages, the chart covers the whole screen instead. Swipe right for the next chart and left to go back (chart_viewer.swipe_right_is_next, and the Swipe chip flips it). Drag the chart slowly with one finger to move the same chart back and forward in time, and pinch with two fingers to zoom (chart_viewer.chart_touch_pan). To change the chart, flick it fast: at least 80 pixels in under 0.3 seconds, and 1.5 times more sideways than up or down (chart_viewer.swipe_min_px, chart_viewer.swipe_max_ms, chart_viewer.swipe_ratio). A slow drag never changes the chart. A swipe on the top row (ticker, price and counter) always changes the chart. On the chip bar, a swipe scrolls the chips when they do not all fit, as on a phone, and changes the chart when they do. The Drag chip switches between Drag: move chart and Drag: next chart, where pinch zoom is off too, and the choice is saved on this device (chart_viewer.drag_mode_toggle). The arrows and the left and right keys work too. The chips show or hide the 10, 20, 50, 150, and 200-day averages and the volume, and the choice is saved on this device. The box in the top left of the chart lists every scanner (chart_viewer.reason_box_top_left; turn it off for the old lower right spot) the stock is on, its status, and its reason. Tap it for more, or hide it with the Reasons chip (chart_viewer.reason_box). The chart loads every saved daily bar, so you can drag back to older days. It opens with thin candles at one width on Daily and Weekly, on every screen (chart_viewer.dense_default, chart_viewer.target_bar_spacing 5.8). Candles never get thinner than 3 pixels or fatter than 8 pixels (chart_viewer.min_bar_spacing_px, chart_viewer.max_bar_spacing_px). A short history stops at 8 pixels instead of stretching, and the empty room stays on the left. Turn dense_default off and Daily opens on the last 6 months, or 3 months on a phone (chart_viewer.range_months, chart_viewer.range_months_phone), and Weekly opens on the last 2 years, or 1 year on a phone (chart_viewer.range_months_weekly, chart_viewer.range_months_weekly_phone). The newest candle sits just left of the price axis with a small gap, in the same spot on every chart (chart_viewer.last_candle_gap_px). With the box in the lower right it sits just left of the Why box instead. A range you dragged to stays when you turn the device or switch full screen. A new chart goes back to the first view. The 3M, 6M, 1Y and All chips are off (chart_viewer.range_chips); drag and pinch move through the history. The Daily and Weekly chips switch the candles (chart_viewer.candle_toggle, chart_viewer.default_candles). Weekly candles are built from the saved daily bars: each week's open, high, low, close and total volume, with the current part week included. The averages are worked out on the bars shown, so on Weekly they are weekly averages. The Candles and Bars chips switch the chart style (chart_viewer.style_toggle, chart_viewer.default_style). Bars are OHLC bars like MarketSmith: a high-low line with a tick on the left for the open and on the right for the close, blue when up and magenta when down. Both choices are saved on this device. The next chart is loaded early so it opens fast. It uses the saved daily bars only. Nothing new is downloaded. Turn the page off with feature.chart_viewer.

The menu splits the screeners into two headings. Technical is price and volume: VCP, Box breakout, Flag breakout, Qullamaggie breakout, Marios breakout, Episodic Pivot, Gap Up, 52-week, 52-week breakouts, High volume, Pullbacks, Trends, and Liquid stocks. Fundamental is the company's numbers and score: CANSLIM, Leaders, Growth, Quality, Dividend, Dividend fundamentals, Stock scorecard, and Top stocks. Market-wide pages (Gainers and losers, Breadth, Sector performance, Heatmaps) are under Market. Today, Buy setups, Trading Floor, Paper Test, the watchlist, the Chart Viewer, earnings, sentiment, macro, and help stay where they were. The Chart Viewer has the same split as a Technical | Fundamental switch. Move a screener to the other heading with scanner_groups in config.json. Turn off only the Chart Viewer switch with chart_viewer.group_toggle: the menu stays split and the Chart Viewer has one All list. Turn the split off with feature.split_tech_fund to get the one combined menu and one All list back.

Every price chart draws its moving averages in the same colors: MA 10 green, MA 20 orange, MA 50 blue, MA 150 yellow, and MA 200 red. That covers the Chart Viewer and the chart that opens under a row on the scanner and list pages. The toggle chips and the legend use the same colors. The row charts' SMA 21 and EMA lines keep their own colors. In light mode the shades are a little darker so each line shows on white (yellow is #ca8a04). Level lines such as Buy point, Entry, Stop, Target, 52w high and low, Hold level, and Trail keep their colors. Change the colors in the chart_colors block (ma_colors, and ma_colors_light for light mode).

The desk starts dark. Pick Dark, Light, or Match device under Theme at the top of the menu (open the menu on a phone). Match device follows the phone or computer setting. The choice is saved on this device only, and the page reloads to switch. Every page, the Chart Viewer, and the charts switch colours. On white, the green, orange, and red labels are darker, and text keeps a contrast of at least 4.5 to 1. Change the starting theme with light_mode.default_theme in config.json (dark, light, or auto). Hide Match device with light_mode.match_device_option. Hide the toggle with feature.light_mode, which keeps every page dark.
Leaders puts a VCP that is ready or broken out today together with a strict CANSLIM qualify. One row per stock.

Edit input/holdings.csv and input/my_watchlist.csv to change the portfolio and the watchlist. Example rows are marked example=yes. Replace them with your own shares and cost. The desk still will not place a trade.
The alerts page lists score and label changes since the last run. It does not send a phone alert, an email, or a message.

OK means the source answered. PARTIAL means a column is blank on every row. CACHED means this run failed and an older copy was used. MISSING means there is no copy at all. A blank cell is missing data. It is not a zero.
Each page starts with a short box that says what the page does. Turn all of them off with feature.page_descriptions in config.json.
Every page has an on/off switch in config.json under features. The index lists have switches under indexes. Turning a page off keeps the file headers so the site does not break.
